exercises.instruction: Choose the correct mixed conditional: past condition → present result.
exercises.prompt: If I ___ that job offer, I ___ in London now.
exercises.explanation: Mixed Type A: past condition (if + had + V3) → present result (would + V1). 'If I had taken that job, I would be in London now.'

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct mixed conditional: present condition → past result.
exercises.prompt: If she ___ so shy, she ___ for the position.
exercises.explanation: Mixed Type B: present condition (if + past simple/were) → past result (would have + V3). She is still shy (present), so she didn't apply (past).

exercises.instruction: Identify the error in the mixed conditional.
exercises.prompt: If I had taken better care of my health, I would feel better now.
options: Should be 'would have felt' — past result needed.
No error — this is a correct mixed conditional (past condition → present result).
Should be 'had felt' — past perfect needed.
Should be 'will feel' — future result needed.
exercises.answer: No error — this is a correct mixed conditional (past condition → present result).
exercises.explanation: 'If I had taken better care' (past perfect) + 'I would feel better now' (would + V1 for present result) = correct Mixed Type A.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct connector: 'unless' = if not.
exercises.prompt: ___ you register in advance, you won't be able to attend.
exercises.explanation: 'If you don't register in advance, you won't be able to attend.' = 'Unless you register in advance, you won't be able to attend.' Both express the same condition.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct conditional connector meaning 'only if'.
exercises.prompt: You may use the equipment, ___ you have completed the safety training.
exercises.explanation: 'Provided that' = on the condition that (only if). It sets a requirement. 'Unless' = if not; 'even if' = regardless; 'in case' = as a precaution.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct use of 'even if'.
exercises.prompt: ___ it rains, we will go ahead with the outdoor event.
exercises.explanation: 'Even if' = despite the condition / regardless of whether. The event will go ahead regardless of rain. 'Even if it rains' = whether or not it rains.

exercises.instruction: Identify the error in the conditional connector sentence.
exercises.prompt: In case you are hungry, you should eat something.
options: Should be 'If you are hungry' — 'in case' means precaution, not condition.
No error — 'in case' is correct here.
Should be 'As long as you are hungry'.
exercises.answer: Should be 'If you are hungry' — 'in case' means precaution, not condition.
exercises.explanation: 'In case' = as a precaution (take an umbrella in case it rains). 'If you are hungry, eat something' = a direct condition. 'In case' ≠ 'if'.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct 'as long as' sentence.
exercises.prompt: You can stay ___ you follow the house rules.
exercises.explanation: 'As long as' = on the condition that / provided that. 'You can stay as long as you follow the rules' = the condition for staying.

exercises.instruction: Which correctly identifies the two types of mixed conditionals?
options: Type A: present condition → past result. Type B: past condition → present result.
Type A: past condition → present result. Type B: present condition → past result.
Both types combine a past perfect if-clause with a would + V1 result.
Mixed conditionals always use 'would have' in the result clause.
exercises.answer: Type A: past condition → present result. Type B: present condition → past result.
exercises.explanation: Type A: if + had + V3 → would + V1 (present). Type B: if + past simple/were → would have + V3 (past). The 'mixed' refers to combining elements from different conditional types.

exercises.instruction: Translate: 'Kecuali kamu belajar, kamu tidak akan lulus.' → English:
exercises.explanation: 'Kecuali' = unless (if not). 'Unless you study, you won't pass' = 'If you don't study, you won't pass.'

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct mixed conditional for: 'I studied medicine (past). I am a doctor now (present).'
exercises.prompt: If I ___ medicine, I ___ a doctor now.
exercises.explanation: Past condition (didn't study medicine) → present result (not a doctor now) → Mixed Type A: if + had + V3, would + V1.

exercises.instruction: Identify the 'even if' vs 'even though' distinction.
options: 'Even if' = despite the fact; 'even though' = whether or not (hypothetical).
'Even if' = hypothetical/future concession; 'even though' = real/known concession.
Both mean exactly the same thing.
'Even if' is formal; 'even though' is informal.
exercises.answer: 'Even if' = hypothetical/future concession; 'even though' = real/known concession.
exercises.explanation: 'Even though it was raining, we continued' (it was raining — fact). 'Even if it rains, we'll continue' (hypothetical — may or may not rain).
'In case it rains' = take the umbrella as a precaution (before you know if it will rain). 'If it rains, take an umbrella' = wait until it rains, then act.

exercises.instruction: Which sentence uses 'whether or not' correctly?
options: I will attend whether or not it is convenient.
I will attend whether or not if it is convenient.
Whether or not I attend, it will convenient.
I whether or not attend will be convenient.
exercises.answer: I will attend whether or not it is convenient.
exercises.explanation: 'Whether or not' = regardless of whether. 'I will attend whether or not it is convenient' — the attendance is unconditional.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct mixed Type B conditional.
exercises.prompt: If he ___ more confident, he ___ for the leadership role last year.
exercises.explanation: Mixed Type B: present condition (if + were/past simple) → past result (would have + V3). He's still not confident (present state) → he didn't apply last year (past).
